title: Sticker price reconciliation for conversational plans
content:
Purpose: quick personal reconcile of what an externally-facing sticker price should mean vs. our internal unit economics for conversational / chat-centric plans. This is a scratch memo — lots of assumptions, leave markers for follow-ups.

Quick context / constraints:
- Target product: hosted API chat plans (per-seat not primary). Focus on per-conversation or per-active-user tiers that combine throughput and latency SLOs.
- Business desiderata: simple external numbers (3–4 tiers), predictable commit options, and a clear rationale for discounts relative to raw per-token pricing.
- Engineering constraints: batching+cache yields effective token cost that varies by workload; heavy short-turn interactive flows are more expensive per useful user minute.

Assumptions (placeholders — update from infra telemetry):
- Baseline GPU effective cost: $6.50 / GPU-hour (blended infra + amortization for hosted).
- Average tokens/sec served on a well-batched stream: 800 tokens/sec per GPU (runtime-optimized for 8-bit quantized model). For conversational workloads with KV cache and prefix reuse, effective tokens/sec can be ~2,400 for certain workloads but not for interactive short-turn. Use conservative 900 tokens/sec for mixed workload.
- Average tokens per conversation minute: 600 tokens/min (12 tokens/sec avg across user input + model output).
- Average active CAU (concurrent active users) handling per GPU: if we budget for latency-first (<=150ms p50), concurrency capacity is the limiting factor. Use a working figure: 40 concurrent interactive streams / GPU.
- Support overhead, infra ops, observability, SRE, licensing tax: 30% markup to raw infra.

First-order unit math (hard-coded example):
- GPU-hour token capacity (conservative): 900 tokens/sec * 3600 sec = 3,240,000 tokens/hour per GPU.
- Effective token cost (infrastructure only): 6.50 / 3,240,000 = $0.000002006 per token (~0.000002). Add 30% ops: $0.0000026 / token.
- Rounding and margin: aim for internal margin before sales/marketing of 50% on hosted API. So list base per-token target = $0.0000052/token.

What this implies for conversational pricing primitives:
- Per-message pricing is noisy (short messages are inefficient). Instead anchor to per-1k-tokens. At $0.0052 / 1k tokens (i.e. $0.0000052/token) we can get to the internal target above. But that feels low compared to market, and doesn't price latency/interactive cost.
- Introduce a latency/interactive premium: a multiplicative surcharge for requests with response latency <200ms or for per-turn P95 <300ms. Rough sketch: +30% surcharge to account for higher concurrency and lower batching efficiency. That would put interactive effective price near $0.00676 / 1k tokens.

Tiering heuristics (3-tier sketch):
- Starter (S): 0–50k tokens / month, price: $0.009 / 1k tokens (includes some overhead; higher to discourage abuse and recover onboarding costs).
- Scale (M): 50k–5M tokens / month, baseline price: $0.0065 / 1k tokens, with auto-tier volume breaks (at >500k tokens drop to $0.0055). But interactive premium applies to low-latency routes.
- Enterprise (E): committed capacity + dedicated pools; pricing: custom but floor $0.004 / 1k tokens (because of dedicated efficiency + contract). Add SLA surcharges and private deployment fees.

Session / active-user packaging alternative (single number):
- Problem: per-token is alien to product folks. One UI-friendly approach is "active minute" bundles: e.g., 1,000 interactive-minutes/month at $X. Convert using tokens/min estimate (600 tokens/min). So 1,000 minutes -> 600k tokens. If baseline price is $0.0065 / 1k tokens -> cost = 0.0065 * 600 = $3.90 per 1,000 minutes. Add rounding/premium -> list at $5 / 1k interactive-min.
- Pros: simpler for buyer to conceptualize. Cons: different workloads will break the conversion (long outputs, attachments).

On commitments and burst allowances:
- Commit model: customers commit to steady monthly baseline (e.g., 100k tokens/month) at a discount (say 20%) vs pay-as-you-go. They can burst above at higher PAYG rate.
- Burst smoothing: offer a 3-day rolling buffer free up to 3x committed throughput to reduce operational frictions. Engineering must track credit burn and excess billing.

Special cases and rate drivers:
- System messages / tool calls: treat deterministically (costed at same token rate but flagged for analytics).
- Multimodal outputs (images + text): price add-on per image generation equivalent (e.g., 100k-token equivalent).
- Latency SLO tiers: 99ms/150ms/300ms p50 anchors with 0/10/20% surcharge respectively. Need to validate with SRE: what does 99ms cost in concurrency headroom?

Quick sensitivity checks:
- If actual tokens/sec is 1,800 (e.g., better batching), infra token cost halves -> internal floor per-1k tokens drops to ~ $0.0026. Implication: room for aggressive discounting for high-volume customers.
- If active concurrency per GPU drops to 20 (more latency sensitive), token capacity halves and cost doubles -> we need dynamic routing or separate "low-latency pool" pricing.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Pull p50/p95 latency vs concurrency curves from runtime (Telemetry ticket JIRA-OBS-298). Need real numbers for latency premium calculation.
- [ ] Update blended GPU-hour cost with current reserved/dedicated pricing mix (Finance spreadsheet link?).
- [ ] Experiment: expose a "low-latency add-on" for routes marked by customer (apply 25–40% surcharge). Validate demand with 10 customers in pilot. Owner: Maya.
- [ ] UX: test "interactive-minute" packaging for non-technical buyers; create 2 landing page variants. Owner: Liam.
- [ ] Legal: confirm that sessionized metric is acceptable for billing terms (avoid confusion around concurrency).

Notes to self / heuristics to keep in mind:
- Don't over-index on raw per-token parity with competitors; our selling point is predictable latency + routing + fallbacks. Buyers will pay a premium for deterministic SLAs.
- Make sure volume-tier math for Scale tier doesn't create perverse incentives (i.e., don't make 500k->501k a cliff). Implement smooth step-downs.
- If we introduce active-minute bundles, limit them to interactive routes only and clearly show token equivalence in the console.

Handy one-liners to keep in pricing docs:
- "Sticker = the price a buyer sees; Unit economics = the story we use to defend that sticker to finance."
- "Latency is a second dimension: price per token should be a function of latency SLO and batching efficiency."

Slack refs (informal):
- slack:#pricing thread "starter vs minutes" (see pinned messages)
- slack:#infra-runtime "kv cache impact notes"

End — keep this as a lightweight anchor. Will iterate after telemetry pull.
